# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RON / notarial gating — fail-closed, nothing approved by default
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class NotApprovedInJurisdiction(PermissionError):
    """Raised when a RON/notarial act is attempted in a jurisdiction
    the owner has not explicitly approved.

    ``code`` is the stable machine-readable error name:
    ``NOT_APPROVED_IN_JURISDICTION``.
    """
    code = "NOT_APPROVED_IN_JURISDICTION"

    def __init__(self, jurisdiction: Any, message: Optional[str] = None):
        self.jurisdiction = jurisdiction
        super().__init__(
            message
            or f"NOT_APPROVED_IN_JURISDICTION: RON/notarial acts are not approved in jurisdiction {jurisdiction!r}. "
            "No jurisdiction is approved by default; owner approval is required."
        )


# The owner-approved set. EMPTY by design: no jurisdiction is approved
# until the owner names it (with legal counsel / verifier confirmation)
# and this set is updated by an explicit owner decision.
APPROVED_RON_JURISDICTIONS: frozenset = frozenset()


def gate_ron(
    jurisdiction: Any,
    *,
    approved: Iterable[str] = APPROVED_RON_JURISDICTIONS,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Fail-closed gate for RON / notarial surfaces.

    Returns ``{"ok": True, "jurisdiction": code}`` only when
    ``jurisdiction`` is a non-empty string present in ``approved``.
    Otherwise raises :class:`NotApprovedInJurisdiction` — including for
    unknown, empty, or missing jurisdictions. ``approved`` must be
    supplied explicitly by the caller when the owner has approved a
    jurisdiction; the module default is empty.
    """
    approved_set = frozenset(
        a.strip().upper() for a in approved if isinstance(a, str) and a.strip()
    )
    if not isinstance(jurisdiction, str) or not jurisdiction.strip():
        raise NotApprovedInJurisdiction(jurisdiction)
    code = jurisdiction.strip().upper()
    if code not in approved_set:
        raise NotApprovedInJurisdiction(code)
    return {"ok": True, "jurisdiction": code}

@dataclass
class ConsentRecord:
    subject_id: str
    scope: str
    granted: bool
    granted_at_utc: Optional[str] = None
    withdrawn_at_utc: Optional[str] = None
    updated_at_utc: str = field(default_factory=utcnow_iso)

    def as_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "subject_id": self.subject_id,
            "scope": self.scope,
            "granted": self.granted,
            "granted_at_utc": self.granted_at_utc,
            "withdrawn_at_utc": self.withdrawn_at_utc,
            "updated_at_utc": self.updated_at_utc,
        }


class ConsentStore:
    """In-memory consent record store.

    This is a record-keeping helper, not durable storage: records live
    in memory for the life of this object. Persisting consent durably
    (SQLite table, retention policy, backup handling) is a declared
    gap — see the audit doc. Scopes are free-form strings such as
    ``"appointment_contact"`` or ``"av_recording"``; no scope is
    granted by default.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._records: Dict[tuple, ConsentRecord] = {}

    @staticmethod
    def _key(subject_id: str, scope: str) -> tuple:
        if not isinstance(subject_id, str) or not subject_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("subject_id must be a non-empty string")
        if not isinstance(scope, str) or not scope.strip():
            raise ValueError("scope must be a non-empty string")
        return (subject_id.strip(), scope.strip())

    def grant(self, subject_id: str, scope: str) -> ConsentRecord:
        now = utcnow_iso()
        record = ConsentRecord(
            subject_id=subject_id.strip(),
            scope=scope.strip(),
            granted=True,
            granted_at_utc=now,
            withdrawn_at_utc=None,
            updated_at_utc=now,
        )
        self._records[self._key(subject_id, scope)] = record
        return record

    def withdraw(self, subject_id: str, scope: str) -> ConsentRecord:
        key = self._key(subject_id, scope)
        now = utcnow_iso()
        existing = self._records.get(key)
        if existing is None:
            record = ConsentRecord(
                subject_id=subject_id.strip(),
                scope=scope.strip(),
                granted=False,
                granted_at_utc=None,
                withdrawn_at_utc=now,
                updated_at_utc=now,
            )
        else:
            record = ConsentRecord(
                subject_id=existing.subject_id,
                scope=existing.scope,
                granted=False,
                granted_at_utc=existing.granted_at_utc,
                withdrawn_at_utc=now,
                updated_at_utc=now,
            )
        self._records[key] = record
        return record

    def status(self, subject_id: str, scope: str) -> Optional[ConsentRecord]:
        return self._records.get(self._key(subject_id, scope))

    def is_granted(self, subject_id: str, scope: str) -> bool:
        record = self.status(subject_id, scope)
        return bool(record and record.granted)

    def all_for_subject(self, subject_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        if not isinstance(subject_id, str):
            raise ValueError("subject_id must be a string")
        subject = subject_id.strip()
        return [
            r.as_dict()
            for (sid, _scope), r in sorted(self._records.items())
            if sid == subject
        ]

class InMemoryRecordStore:
    """A tiny fake record store used by tests and as the adapter shape
    for real stores. Records are plain dicts that must carry the
    subject's id under ``subject_id``. Real stores (SQLite ledgers,
    case registries) are NOT wired here — that is a declared gap."""

    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self._records: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    def add(self, record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
        self._records.append(dict(record))

    def export_for(self, subject_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        return [dict(r) for r in self._records if r.get("subject_id") == subject_id]

    def delete_for(self, subject_id: str) -> int:
        before = len(self._records)
        self._records = [r for r in self._records if r.get("subject_id") != subject_id]
        return before - len(self._records)


class DataSubjectRequestHandler:
    """Handles data export and deletion requests against adapters.

    A store adapter is any object with ``name`` and ``export_for``;
    deletion additionally requires ``delete_for``. Stores without
    ``delete_for`` (or whose ``delete_for`` raises
    ``NotImplementedError``) are reported honestly as
    ``NOT_IMPLEMENTED`` — the request itself is still recorded with a
    stable ``request_id`` so the owner can follow it up. This handler
    never claims deletion from systems it cannot reach (provider
    dashboards, backups, third-party platforms).
    """

    def __init__(self, stores: Iterable[Any] = ()) -> None:
        self._stores: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for store in stores:
            self._stores[store.name] = store
        self._requests: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    def register_store(self, store: Any) -> None:
        self._stores[store.name] = store

    def export_subject_data(self, subject_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if not isinstance(subject_id, str) or not subject_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("subject_id must be a non-empty string")
        subject_id = subject_id.strip()
        stores_out: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for name, store in sorted(self._stores.items()):
            export_for = getattr(store, "export_for", None)
            if export_for is None:
                stores_out[name] = {
                    "status": "NOT_IMPLEMENTED",
                    "records": [],
                    "note": "Store has no export_for adapter.",
                }
            else:
                stores_out[name] = {
                    "status": "EXPORTED",
                    "records": export_for(subject_id),
                }
        result = {
            "subject_id": subject_id,
            "exported_at_utc": utcnow_iso(),
            "stores": stores_out,
            "note": "Export covers only the registered stores above. Backups, provider dashboards, and third-party platforms are not included.",
        }
        self._requests.append({"type": "export", **result})
        return result

    def request_deletion(self, subject_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if not isinstance(subject_id, str) or not subject_id.strip():
            raise ValueError("subject_id must be a non-empty string")
        subject_id = subject_id.strip()
        per_store: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for name, store in sorted(self._stores.items()):
            delete_for = getattr(store, "delete_for", None)
            if delete_for is None:
                per_store[name] = {
                    "status": "NOT_IMPLEMENTED",
                    "deleted_count": 0,
                    "note": "Store has no delete_for adapter; nothing was deleted here.",
                }
                continue
            try:
                deleted = delete_for(subject_id)
            except NotImplementedError:
                per_store[name] = {
                    "status": "NOT_IMPLEMENTED",
                    "deleted_count": 0,
                    "note": "Store reports deletion as not implemented.",
                }
                continue
            per_store[name] = {
                "status": "DELETED",
                "deleted_count": int(deleted),
                "note": "Records deleted from this store only. Backups and third-party copies are not covered.",
            }
        result = {
            "request_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "type": "deletion",
            "subject_id": subject_id,
            "requested_at_utc": utcnow_iso(),
            "status": "RECORDED",
            "per_store": per_store,
            "note": "Request recorded. NOT_IMPLEMENTED stores still hold the subject's records and need owner follow-up.",
        }
        self._requests.append(result)
        return result

    def recorded_requests(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        return [dict(r) for r in self._requests]

    def export_json(self, subject_id: str) -> str:
        """Export as a JSON string (the portable export format)."""
        return json.dumps(self.export_subject_data(subject_id), indent=2, sort_keys=True)

# Each item: (id, WCAG 2.2 criterion, name, what counts as evidence).
WCAG_CHECKLIST: List[Dict[str, str]] = [
    {"id": "a11y-lang", "criterion": "3.1.1", "name": "Page has a lang attribute",
     "evidence": "html lang attribute present (e.g. <html lang=\"en\">)"},
    {"id": "a11y-alt", "criterion": "1.1.1", "name": "Images have alt text",
     "evidence": "every <img> carries an alt attribute"},
    {"id": "a11y-labels", "criterion": "1.3.1 / 3.3.2", "name": "Form inputs have labels",
     "evidence": "every input/select/textarea has an associated <label for=id> or aria-label"},
    {"id": "a11y-buttons", "criterion": "4.1.2", "name": "Buttons have accessible names",
     "evidence": "every <button> has visible text or an aria-label"},
    {"id": "a11y-live", "criterion": "4.1.3", "name": "Status messages use live regions",
     "evidence": "status/feedback containers use role=status and aria-live"},
    {"id": "a11y-keyboard", "criterion": "2.1.1", "name": "All functionality keyboard-operable",
     "evidence": "manual keyboard walkthrough of the page — cannot be proven by static HTML alone"},
    {"id": "a11y-focus", "criterion": "2.4.7", "name": "Keyboard focus is visible",
     "evidence": "visible :focus styles exist and focus is never removed with outline:none alone"},
    {"id": "a11y-contrast", "criterion": "1.4.3", "name": "Text contrast >= 4.5:1 (normal text)",
     "evidence": "measured contrast ratio for body text — cannot be proven by static HTML alone"},
    {"id": "a11y-target", "criterion": "2.5.8", "name": "Pointer targets >= 24x24 CSS px",
     "evidence": "measured target sizes — cannot be proven by static HTML alone"},
    {"id": "a11y-skip", "criterion": "2.4.1", "name": "Skip link / bypass block present",
     "evidence": "a skip-to-content link exists on pages with repeated navigation"},
]

_IMG_RE = re.compile(r"<img\b[^>]*>", re.IGNORECASE)
_ALT_RE = re.compile(r"""alt\s*=\s*("[^"]*"|'[^']*')""", re.IGNORECASE)
_LANG_RE = re.compile(r"<html\b[^>]*\blang\s*=\s*[\"'][^\"']+[\"']", re.IGNORECASE)
_INPUT_RE = re.compile(
    r"<(input|select|textarea)\b([^>]*)>", re.IGNORECASE)
_ID_RE = re.compile(r"""\bid\s*=\s*("[^"]*"|'[^']*')""", re.IGNORECASE)
_LABEL_FOR_RE = re.compile(
    r"""<label\b[^>]*\bfor\s*=\s*("[^"]*"|'[^']*')""", re.IGNORECASE)
_ARIA_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"""aria-label\s*=\s*("[^"]*"|'[^']*')""", re.IGNORECASE)
_BUTTON_RE = re.compile(r"<button\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</button>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
_SKIP_RE = re.compile(r"skip", re.IGNORECASE)


def _strip_quotes(value: str) -> str:
    return value.strip().strip("\"'")


def check_html_accessibility(html: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Static accessibility checks over an HTML string.

    Only the statically checkable items (lang, alt, labels, button
    names, live regions, skip link) are decided here. Items needing a
    human or a browser measurement (keyboard walkthrough, focus
    visibility, contrast, target size) are honestly reported as
    ``not_checked`` with the reason recorded. ``html`` must be a
    string; anything else raises ``ValueError``.
    """
    if not isinstance(html, str):
        raise ValueError("html must be a string")
    results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    def verdict(item_id: str, outcome: str, detail: str) -> None:
        item = next(i for i in WCAG_CHECKLIST if i["id"] == item_id)
        results.append({
            "id": item["id"],
            "criterion": item["criterion"],
            "name": item["name"],
            "result": outcome,  # pass | fail | not_checked
            "detail": detail,
        })

    # lang
    verdict("a11y-lang",
            "pass" if _LANG_RE.search(html) else "fail",
            "html lang attribute present" if _LANG_RE.search(html)
            else "no <html lang=...> attribute found")

    # alt text
    imgs = _IMG_RE.findall(html)
    missing_alt = [t for t in imgs if not _ALT_RE.search(t)]
    if not imgs:
        verdict("a11y-alt", "not_checked", "no <img> elements on the page")
    elif not missing_alt:
        verdict("a11y-alt", "pass", f"{len(imgs)} image(s), all with alt")
    else:
        verdict("a11y-alt", "fail",
                f"{len(missing_alt)} of {len(imgs)} image(s) missing alt")

    # labels
    label_targets = {_strip_quotes(m) for m in _LABEL_FOR_RE.findall(html)}
    unlabeled: List[str] = []
    for _tag, attrs in _INPUT_RE.findall(html):
        if _ARIA_LABEL_RE.search(attrs):
            continue
        m = _ID_RE.search(attrs)
        if m and _strip_quotes(m.group(1)) in label_targets:
            continue
        if re.search(r"""\btype\s*=\s*["']?(hidden|submit|button)["']?""",
                     attrs, re.IGNORECASE):
            continue
        unlabeled.append(attrs.strip()[:60])
    inputs = _INPUT_RE.findall(html)
    if not inputs:
        verdict("a11y-labels", "not_checked", "no form fields on the page")
    elif not unlabeled:
        verdict("a11y-labels", "pass",
                f"{len(inputs)} field(s), all labelled")
    else:
        verdict("a11y-labels", "fail",
                f"{len(unlabeled)} field(s) without a label: {unlabeled[:3]}")

    # buttons
    buttons = _BUTTON_RE.findall(html)
    unnamed = [a for a, text in buttons
               if not text.strip() and not _ARIA_LABEL_RE.search(a)]
    if not buttons:
        verdict("a11y-buttons", "not_checked", "no <button> elements on the page")
    elif not unnamed:
        verdict("a11y-buttons", "pass", f"{len(buttons)} button(s), all named")
    else:
        verdict("a11y-buttons", "fail",
                f"{len(unnamed)} of {len(buttons)} button(s) without a name")

    # live regions
    has_live = bool(re.search(r"""role\s*=\s*["']status["']""", html, re.IGNORECASE)
                    or re.search(r"""aria-live\s*=\s*["']polite["']""", html, re.IGNORECASE))
    verdict("a11y-live",
            "pass" if has_live else "not_checked",
            "role=status / aria-live region found" if has_live
            else "no live region found in static HTML; status-message behaviour not verified")

    # skip link
    verdict("a11y-skip",
            "pass" if _SKIP_RE.search(html) else "not_checked",
            "skip link text found" if _SKIP_RE.search(html)
            else "no skip link found in static HTML; bypass behaviour not verified")

    # Items that cannot be decided from static HTML.
    for item_id, reason in (
        ("a11y-keyboard", "needs a manual keyboard walkthrough in a browser"),
        ("a11y-focus", "needs rendered :focus styles checked in a browser"),
        ("a11y-contrast", "needs measured contrast ratios, not source text"),
        ("a11y-target", "needs measured target sizes, not source text"),
    ):
        verdict(item_id, "not_checked", reason)

    passed = sum(1 for r in results if r["result"] == "pass")
    failed = [r for r in results if r["result"] == "fail"]
    return {
        "checked_at_utc": utcnow_iso(),
        "total_items": len(results),
        "passed": passed,
        "failed": len(failed),
        "not_checked": sum(1 for r in results if r["result"] == "not_checked"),
        "items": results,
        "summary": (
            "FAIL: " + ", ".join(f"{f['id']} ({f['criterion']})" for f in failed)
            if failed else
            "No static failures found; unchecked items still need a real audit."
        ),
    }


class AccessibilityChecklist:
    """Evidence-based WCAG 2.2 AA checklist.

    ``check_page`` takes an evidence mapping (one boolean / value per
    item id, or ``None`` when unknown) and reports pass / fail /
    not_checked honestly: an item with no evidence is ``not_checked``,
    never assumed to pass. ``check_html`` runs the static checks in
    :func:`check_html_accessibility` for a page's HTML source.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def check_page(evidence: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if not isinstance(evidence, Mapping):
            raise ValueError("evidence must be a mapping of item id -> evidence")
        items: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for entry in WCAG_CHECKLIST:
            value = evidence.get(entry["id"], None)
            if value is None:
                result, detail = "not_checked", "no evidence supplied"
            elif value is True:
                result, detail = "pass", "evidence supplied: pass"
            elif value is False:
                result, detail = "fail", "evidence supplied: fail"
            else:
                result, detail = "not_checked", f"evidence supplied but not a pass/fail boolean: {value!r}"
            items.append({
                "id": entry["id"],
                "criterion": entry["criterion"],
                "name": entry["name"],
                "result": result,
                "detail": detail,
            })
        failed = [i for i in items if i["result"] == "fail"]
        return {
            "checked_at_utc": utcnow_iso(),
            "total_items": len(items),
            "passed": sum(1 for i in items if i["result"] == "pass"),
            "failed": len(failed),
            "not_checked": sum(1 for i in items if i["result"] == "not_checked"),
            "items": items,
            "summary": (
                "FAIL: " + ", ".join(f"{f['id']} ({f['criterion']})" for f in failed)
                if failed else
                "No failures in the evidence supplied; unchecked items still need a real audit."
            ),
        }

    @staticmethod
    def check_html(html: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return check_html_accessibility(html)

core_platform/global_connectivity.py.content:
"""Real-world connectivity policy for Sanders Dash & Seal (added 2026-11-13).

Per-region latency / timeout / retry / backoff policy for the real-time
platforms, with the offline / free-first fallback declared for each one.
Stdlib only. Fakes only: this module makes no network calls, holds no
keys, and performs no live call. It is a *policy table* plus a pure
backoff computation — the numbers below are policy, not measured
latency. No measured latency is claimed anywhere here.

Free-first / Always Free order (owner direction, Core Law 10/11):
Oracle Always Free (us-phoenix-1) is the deployment home first; local
free options (faster-whisper, system TTS, self-hosted LiveKit) are
tried before any paid provider call; a paid provider is only used when
its key is configured by the owner and the free path cannot serve the
request. This module declares the order — it does not perform the
fallback, because no live transport exists in this worktree snapshot
(``core_platform/openai_link.py`` and ``core_platform/realtime_api.py``
live on the link branches, not in snapshot 4342b230).

Timeouts below are per-attempt ceilings, not guarantees. Retries use
exponential backoff with a cap; the backoff function is pure and
deterministic (no jitter randomness) so tests can assert on it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, List

__all__ = [
    "PLATFORMS",
    "REGIONS",
    "RegionPolicy",
    "backoff_seconds",
    "fallback_for",
    "policy_for",
]

REGIONS: frozenset = frozenset({"us", "eu", "apac"})

# Primary deployment region is us-phoenix-1 (Oracle Always Free).
# "eu" / "apac" policies exist so a future region can be configured;
# no EU/APAC deployment exists today, so those policies are declared
# but unproven — see the compliance audit doc.
REGION_NOTES: Dict[str, str] = {
    "us": "Primary. Oracle Always Free us-phoenix-1. Only region with a deployed instance.",
    "eu": "Declared only. No EU region deployed; EEA data residency is NOT_IMPLEMENTED.",
    "apac": "Declared only. No APAC region deployed.",
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RegionPolicy:
    platform: str
    region: str
    timeout_seconds: float
    max_retries: int
    backoff_base_seconds: float
    backoff_max_seconds: float
    offline_fallback: str
    notes: str = ""


def _policy(platform: str, region: str, timeout: float, retries: int,
            base: float, cap: float, fallback: str, notes: str = "") -> RegionPolicy:
    return RegionPolicy(
        platform=platform, region=region, timeout_seconds=timeout,
        max_retries=retries, backoff_base_seconds=base,
        backoff_max_seconds=cap, offline_fallback=fallback, notes=notes,
    )

# (core_platform/daedalus_claude_transport.py). STT/TTS are shorter

def policy_for(platform: str, region: str = "us") -> RegionPolicy:
    """Return the connectivity policy for ``platform`` in ``region``.

    Raises ``ValueError`` for an unknown platform or region — an
    unlisted platform has no timeout/retry policy and must not be
    called on an invented one.
    """
    if not isinstance(platform, str) or platform.strip().lower() not in PLATFORMS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown platform: {platform!r}. Known: {sorted(PLATFORMS)}")
    if not isinstance(region, str) or region.strip().lower() not in REGIONS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown region: {region!r}. Known: {sorted(REGIONS)}")
    return PLATFORMS[platform.strip().lower()][region.strip().lower()]


def fallback_for(platform: str, region: str = "us") -> str:
    """The declared offline / free-first fallback for a platform."""
    return policy_for(platform, region).offline_fallback


def backoff_seconds(attempt: int, *, base: float = 1.0, cap: float = 8.0) -> float:
    """Exponential backoff delay before retry number ``attempt``.

    ``attempt`` is 1-based (first retry waits ``base``). Pure and
    deterministic: ``min(base * 2 ** (attempt - 1), cap)``. Raises
    ``ValueError`` for ``attempt < 1`` or non-positive ``base``/``cap``.
    """
    if not isinstance(attempt, int) or attempt < 1:
        raise ValueError("attempt must be a positive integer (1-based retry number)")
    if base <= 0 or cap <= 0:
        raise ValueError("base and cap must be positive")
    return min(base * (2 ** (attempt - 1)), cap)


def all_policies() -> List[RegionPolicy]:
    """Every declared policy, sorted by platform then region."""
    return [PLATFORMS[p][r] for p in sorted(PLATFORMS) for r in sorted(PLATFORMS[p])]

core_platform/global_payments.py.content:
"""Multi-currency payments for Sanders Dash & Seal (global, real-world).

Stdlib only. No network, no live calls, no keys, no Stripe SDK import.

What this module does
---------------------
* Currency is always an explicit, validated ISO 4217 code from an
  allowlist of Stripe-supported currencies.  There is no silent
  default: USD is used only when the caller passes it explicitly as
  ``fallback_currency="USD"`` (see :func:`resolve_currency`).
* Money is always integer minor units (cents, yen, fils, ...).
  Float money is rejected outright; amounts are ``int`` / ``str`` /
  ``Decimal`` only.  Zero-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW, ...) and
  three-decimal currencies (BHD, KWD, ...) use their ISO 4217
  minor-unit exponent, so JPY 500 is 500 minor units, not 50000.
* Amounts are formatted per locale from an explicit locale table
  (no ``babel``, no system-locale dependence).
* Tax / VAT is NOT computed.  There is no tax engine and no VAT
  rates in this codebase.  Anything that asks for tax fails honestly
  with :class:`TaxNotImplementedError` / ``TAX_NOT_IMPLEMENTED``.
  Rates must never be invented here.

What this module does NOT do
----------------------------
* It does not call Stripe, charge a card, or verify a webhook
  signature.  Signature verification stays in
  ``core_platform.stripe_payments.verify_stripe_webhook`` and the
  WSGI webhook apps.  :func:`build_stripe_checkout_params` only
  builds the parameter dict a caller would hand to a Stripe client
  in test mode; :func:`validate_webhook_event` only validates the
  currency/amount/livemode fields of an already-verified event dict.
* It does not change live behaviour.  Live Stripe is gated:
  ``livemode=True`` requires ``live_verified=True`` as well
  (the ``STRIPE_LIVEMODE=true`` AND ``STRIPE_LIVE_VERIFIED=true``
  pair).  No live Stripe keys exist in this repo; nothing here
  creates or reads one.
* It does not fix the existing USD-only paths in place.  The audit
  (``GLOBAL_PAYMENTS_AUDIT_20261113.md`` at the worktree root)
  lists them; ``core_platform/appointment_payments.py`` still
  hardcodes ``'usd'`` and ``core_platform/stripe_payments.py``
  still does not check event currency against the stored currency.
  This module is the replacement primitive those paths should
  adopt, subject to owner/verifier approval -- it is not wired
  into them by this change.

Wiring point (for the owner/verifier, not applied here)
-------------------------------------------------------
In the test-mode webhook path (``core_platform/stream_api.py``,
``import_make_app`` with ``expected_livemode=False``), after the
signature check and before ledger settlement, call::

    from core_platform.global_payments import validate_webhook_event
    checked = validate_webhook_event(event, expected_livemode=False)

and, where a checkout was registered, also pass the expected
``expected_amount_minor`` / ``expected_currency`` so a currency
mismatch cannot settle silently (the current
``stripe_payments.PaymentLedger.record_event`` checks amount only).
Do not wire this into any live-mode path until live is verified.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation

__all__ = [
    "SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES",
    "ZERO_DECIMAL_CURRENCIES",
    "THREE_DECIMAL_CURRENCIES",
    "TAX_STATUS",
    "GlobalPaymentError",
    "CurrencyError",
    "TaxNotImplementedError",
    "LivePaymentDenied",
    "normalize_currency",
    "minor_unit_exponent",
    "is_zero_decimal_currency",
    "to_minor_units",
    "from_minor_units",
    "format_amount",
    "resolve_currency",
    "calculate_tax",
    "tax_status",
    "quote_total",
    "build_stripe_checkout_params",
    "validate_webhook_event",
    "annotate_test_mode_event",
    "describe_scenario_total",
    "live_gate",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Errors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class GlobalPaymentError(ValueError):
    """Base error for this module.  A ValueError so callers can catch broadly."""


class CurrencyError(GlobalPaymentError):
    """Unknown, malformed, or unsupported currency / locale / amount."""


class TaxNotImplementedError(GlobalPaymentError, NotImplementedError):
    """Tax was requested but no tax engine exists.  See TAX_STATUS."""


class LivePaymentDenied(GlobalPaymentError):
    """A live-mode payment was requested without the live verification gate."""


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Currency allowlist
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conservative allowlist of Stripe-supported ISO 4217 codes, as of
# 2026-11-13 (Stripe's supported-currencies list).  Deliberately
# conservative: a currency missing here is rejected honestly instead
# of being accepted and mis-priced.  Re-verify against Stripe's
# current list before any live use; do not silently extend it.
# HRK is excluded (Croatia adopted the euro in 2023).
SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES = frozenset(
    {
        "AED", "AFN", "ALL", "AMD", "ANG", "AOA", "ARS", "AUD", "AWG",
        "AZN", "BAM", "BBD", "BDT", "BGN", "BHD", "BIF", "BMD", "BND",
        "BOB", "BRL", "BSD", "BTN", "BWP", "BYN", "BZD", "CAD", "CDF",
        "CHF", "CLP", "CNY", "COP", "CRC", "CVE", "CZK", "DJF", "DKK",
        "DOP", "DZD", "EGP", "ERN", "ETB", "EUR", "FJD", "FKP", "GBP",
        "GEL", "GHS", "GIP", "GMD", "GNF", "GTQ", "GYD", "HKD", "HNL",
        "HTG", "HUF", "IDR", "ILS", "IMP", "INR", "IQD", "IRR", "ISK",
        "JEP", "JMD", "JOD", "JPY", "KES", "KGS", "KHR", "KMF", "KRW",
        "KWD", "KYD", "KZT", "LAK", "LBP", "LKR", "LRD", "LSL", "LYD",
        "MAD", "MDL", "MGA", "MKD", "MMK", "MNT", "MOP", "MRU", "MUR",
        "MVR", "MWK", "MXN", "MYR", "MZN", "NAD", "NGN", "NIO", "NOK",
        "NPR", "NZD", "OMR", "PAB", "PEN", "PGK", "PHP", "PKR", "PLN",
        "PYG", "QAR", "RON", "RSD", "RWF", "SAR", "SBD", "SCR", "SDG",
        "SEK", "SGD", "SHP", "SLE", "SLL", "SOS", "SRD", "SSP", "STN",
        "SYP", "SZL", "THB", "TJS", "TMT", "TND", "TOP", "TRY", "TTD",
        "TWD", "TZS", "UAH", "UGX", "USD", "UYU", "UZS", "VES", "VND",
        "VUV", "WST", "XAF", "XCD", "XOF", "XPF", "YER", "ZAR", "ZMW",
        "ZWL",
    }
)

# Stripe zero-decimal currencies: amounts are whole units, no cents.
ZERO_DECIMAL_CURRENCIES = frozenset(
    {
        "BIF", "CLP", "DJF", "GNF", "JPY", "KMF", "KRW", "MGA", "PYG",
        "RWF", "UGX", "VND", "VUV", "XAF", "XOF", "XPF",
    }
)

# ISO 4217 three-decimal currencies (1 unit = 1000 minor units).
THREE_DECIMAL_CURRENCIES = frozenset(
    {"BHD", "IQD", "JOD", "KWD", "LYD", "OMR", "TND"}
)

TAX_STATUS = "TAX_NOT_IMPLEMENTED"


def normalize_currency(code) -> str:
    """Validate and normalise a currency code to upper-case ISO 4217.

    Raises :class:`CurrencyError` for anything not on the allowlist
    -- including well-formed but unsupported codes, so a typo can
    never silently become a different currency.
    """
    if not isinstance(code, str):
        raise CurrencyError("Currency code must be a string, got %r" % type(code).__name__)
    cleaned = code.strip().upper()
    if len(cleaned) != 3 or not cleaned.isalpha():
        raise CurrencyError("Currency code must be three letters, got %r" % code)
    if cleaned not in SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES:
        raise CurrencyError("Unsupported currency %r: not on the Stripe-supported allowlist" % cleaned)
    return cleaned


def minor_unit_exponent(currency: str) -> int:
    """Minor-unit exponent for a currency: 0, 2, or 3."""
    code = normalize_currency(currency)
    if code in ZERO_DECIMAL_CURRENCIES:
        return 0
    if code in THREE_DECIMAL_CURRENCIES:
        return 3
    return 2


def is_zero_decimal_currency(currency: str) -> bool:
    return normalize_currency(currency) in ZERO_DECIMAL_CURRENCIES


def _to_decimal(amount, *, what: str = "amount") -> Decimal:
    """Exact Decimal from int/str/Decimal only.  Floats are rejected:
    float money is never exact, so it is never accepted here."""
    if isinstance(amount, bool):
        raise CurrencyError("%s must not be a bool" % what)
    if isinstance(amount, float):
        raise CurrencyError(
            "%s must not be a float: float money is inexact; pass int, str or Decimal" % what
        )
    if isinstance(amount, Decimal):
        value = amount
    elif isinstance(amount, int):
        value = Decimal(amount)
    elif isinstance(amount, str):
        try:
            value = Decimal(amount.strip())
        except (InvalidOperation, ValueError, AttributeError):
            raise CurrencyError("%s is not a valid decimal amount: %r" % (what, amount)) from None
    else:
        raise CurrencyError(
            "%s must be int, str or Decimal, got %r" % (what, type(amount).__name__)
        )
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise CurrencyError("%s must be finite" % what)
    return value


def to_minor_units(amount, currency: str) -> int:
    """Convert a major-unit amount to integer minor units, exactly.

    ``to_minor_units("10.99", "USD") == 1099``;
    ``to_minor_units("500", "JPY") == 500`` (zero-decimal);
    ``to_minor_units("1.234", "BHD") == 1234`` (three-decimal).
    An amount with more decimal places than the currency allows
    (e.g. ``"10.999"`` USD, ``"500.5"`` JPY) raises
    :class:`CurrencyError` instead of being rounded -- rounding
    money silently is a pricing error.  Negative amounts raise.
    """
    code = normalize_currency(currency)
    value = _to_decimal(amount)
    if value < 0:
        raise CurrencyError("Amount must not be negative: %r" % (amount,))
    exponent = minor_unit_exponent(code)
    quantum = Decimal(1).scaleb(-exponent)
    if value != value.quantize(quantum):
        raise CurrencyError(
            "Amount %r has more decimal places than %s allows (exponent %d)"
            % (amount, code, exponent)
        )
    return int(value.scaleb(exponent))


def from_minor_units(minor_units: int, currency: str) -> Decimal:
    """Convert integer minor units back to a major-unit Decimal."""
    code = normalize_currency(currency)
    if isinstance(minor_units, bool) or not isinstance(minor_units, int):
        raise CurrencyError("Minor units must be an int, got %r" % type(minor_units).__name__)
    if minor_units < 0:
        raise CurrencyError("Minor units must not be negative")
    return Decimal(minor_units).scaleb(-minor_unit_exponent(code))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Locale handling: currency resolution + formatting (explicit tables only)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Exact locale (language-REGION) -> currency.  Language alone is NOT
# mapped: "es" could be EUR (Spain) or MXN (Mexico), so only a full
# locale resolves.  Unknown locales resolve to nothing (see below).
_LOCALE_CURRENCY = {
    "ar-AE": "AED", "ar-SA": "SAR", "cs-CZ": "CZK", "da-DK": "DKK",
    "de-AT": "EUR", "de-DE": "EUR", "el-GR": "EUR", "en-AU": "AUD",
    "en-CA": "CAD", "en-GB": "GBP", "en-IE": "EUR", "en-IN": "INR",
    "en-NZ": "NZD", "en-US": "USD", "en-ZA": "ZAR", "es-ES": "EUR",
    "es-MX": "MXN", "fi-FI": "EUR", "fr-BE": "EUR", "fr-FR": "EUR",
    "he-IL": "ILS", "hu-HU": "HUF", "id-ID": "IDR", "it-IT": "EUR",
    "ja-JP": "JPY", "ko-KR": "KRW", "ms-MY": "MYR", "nb-NO": "NOK",
    "nl-NL": "EUR", "pl-PL": "PLN", "pt-BR": "BRL", "pt-PT": "EUR",

# fr-FR uses a non-breaking space before the symbol (French convention).

    "en-US": (".", ",", True, False, " "),

    "it-IT": (",", ".", False, True, " "),

    "CNY": "¥", "CZK": "Kč", "DKK": "kr", "EUR": "€", "GBP": "£",
